messages:
sophia: Anyone else seeing a perf regression in the page-fusion FlashAttention variant when KV cache is interleaved? p99 went up ~10-15% after the bfloat16 rollout.

infra-bot: [perf-alert] nightly/regression: +12% p99 on chat-gen (pagefusion-flash, interleaved-kv) — see dashboard link: https://perf.internal/redwood/alerts/1798501234

raj: I repro'd locally. Small microbench (seq_len=512, batch=8, kv_interleaved=true) shows kernel launch falling back to slower path with bigger l2 reads. nvprof snippet: 
```
Kernel: flash_fused_bf16_pagefusion
Time: 2.3ms (hot) -> 2.6ms after change
Global load throughput drops ~25%
```

felix: Interesting — could be misaligned loads from interleaved layout causing vectorized loads to degrade. What is the stride/dtype?

raj: Layout is interleaved: [batch, heads, seq, head_dim] packed, dtype=bfloat16. Head_dim=64 (but we recently allowed odd padding for memory packing, so some tensors now have stride not divisible by 64bytes).

morgan: If head_dim*bytes_per_elem isn't 64B-aligned then our fused kernels that assume 64B alignment will hit slow paths (unaligned ld/st). We did a small change in allocator to remove padding for memory savings — might be culprit.

felix: Can you paste the stride info from a failing run? i.e. torch_tensor.stride() and storage_offset?

raj: Paste below from reproducer: 
```
kv.shape: (8, 16, 512, 64)
kv.stride: (524288, 32768, 64, 1)
storage_offset: 0
bytes_per_elem: 2
row_bytes = head_dim * 2 = 128 bytes -> looks aligned, but after interleaving shuffle we end up with stride 66 in a few cases due to compacting logic.
```

sophia: So it's not always happening, only on certain sequences/packing combos. That matches nightly spike being intermittent. Could be our compacting + dtype promotion path.

morgan: I ran a quick perf counter: L2 read bandwidth spikes and global load efficiency drops when stride % 32 != 0. Also saw more serialized __ldg instructions on sm_86.

felix: Hypothesis: when head_dim padding removed, the inner-loop loads use unaligned 128-bit ld which on some GPUs becomes multiple narrower loads. Two mitigations: 1) force pad_to = 32 elements (64B) on allocation for KV when using fused/pagefusion kernels; 2) update kernels to use byte-wise memcpy fallback for unaligned but optimized path.

raj: I tried option 1 locally: padding to 32 elements brings kernel back to baseline; p99 reduced and memory usage +0.6%. Patch diff below: 
```diff
- alloc_kv(head_dim)
+ alloc_kv(pad_to(head_dim, 32))
```

morgan: Good quick win. But we need to validate effect on Dedicated nodes where memory is tight. Also check that quantized flows (int8) don't regress because padding multiplies memory delta.

felix: Next steps: I'll run targeted benchmarks across variants: pagefusion-flash, fused-flash, and paged-attn with interleaved/separate KV, dtype={bf16,fp16,int8} for seq_len in {128,512,1024} and batch sizes {1,8,32}. I’ll include nvprof and Nsight traces to capture L2/GDR stats.

sophia: Great. Raj: please produce a minimal reproducer script for CI perf tests (single-file) and add a quick opt-in flag to enable pad_to behaviour. Morgan: run memory impact numbers for 1/10/100 instances and report. Felix: target to have kernel fallback patch or allocator guard by EOD tomorrow.

raj: Reproducer posted to /tmp/pagefusion_repro.py and pushed to branch: feature/kv-align-pad. It toggles interleaved layout and prints torch.storage().size() and stride.

morgan: I'll run memory sweep on Dedicated cluster tonight and post results in this thread.

felix: One more note — batching heuristics interplay: when we batch many short sequences we hit random alignment combos. Recommend in the short term to prefer separate-KV layout for small head_dim variants in batcher heuristics (config flag: prefer_separate_kv_small_heads=true).

sophia: Agree. Add that heuristic to the batching layer as a stopgap. We'll follow up with kernel-level fixes. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: [action] felix assigned: run cross-variant matrix + trace (due: 2026-03-19)
infra-bot: [action] raj assigned: add reproducer + opt-in pad flag (due: 2026-03-18)
infra-bot: [action] morgan assigned: mem-sweep on Dedicated (due: 2026-03-18)

sophia: Thanks all. Let's reconvene after the traces land. If anyone finds a cheap kernel trick to mask unaligned loads, ping here.
